d: Any method that delivers an estrogen, usually ethinyl estradiol, together with a progestin: the pill, the weekly patch and the monthly vaginal ring. All three share the estrogen contraindications.

How well a method works as people actually use it, including missed pills and late injections. It is the number used in counseling, and it differs most from perfect use for methods that depend on the user.
The etonogestrel implant and the levonorgestrel and copper IUDs. They last years, need no action from the user, and fail in fewer than 1 in 100 women a year with typical use.
A drug that increases hepatic CYP3A4 activity, such as rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin or St John's wort. Contraceptive steroids are then cleared faster, and their levels fall.

A drug that acts as a progesterone agonist in some tissues and an antagonist in others. Ulipristal is the emergency contraceptive in this class; it can delay follicle rupture even after LH starts to rise.

Unscheduled bleeding or spotting during active hormone use. It is the most common adverse effect of hormonal contraception and usually settles within 3 months. Persistent bleeding calls for a check for pregnancy, infection and structural causes.
